title: "Micah"

# Micah

::: {.book-summary}
## Book Summary Insight

Micah alternates between judgment and hope while announcing the coming Messiah from Bethlehem. The book teaches that God desires justice, mercy, and humble fellowship with Him.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 1

<div class="key-verse">Micah 1:2</div>

<div class="identifier">Hear, all ye people</div>

### Why This Verse

Opening prophetic summons

### Chapter Insight

This chapter announces God's judgment against Samaria and Jerusalem. The key verse emphasizes that God sees and responds to the sins of His people.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 2

<div class="key-verse">Micah 2:13</div>

<div class="identifier">The breaker is come up before them</div>

### Why This Verse

Messianic interpretation

### Chapter Insight

This chapter condemns oppression, greed, and exploitation. The key verse highlights God's concern for justice and the protection of the vulnerable.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 3

<div class="key-verse">Micah 3:8</div>

<div class="identifier">I am full of power by the Spirit of the LORD</div>

### Why This Verse

Prophetic authority

### Chapter Insight

This chapter rebukes corrupt leaders, priests, and prophets. The key verse demonstrates that leadership without righteousness invites God's judgment.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 4

<div class="key-verse">Micah 4:3</div>

<div class="identifier">They shall beat their swords into plowshares</div>

### Why This Verse

Famous peace prophecy

### Chapter Insight

This chapter promises future peace and restoration under God's reign. The key verse envisions the nations coming to the Lord and learning His ways.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 5

<div class="key-verse">Micah 5:2</div>

<div class="identifier">Bethlehem Ephratah</div>

### Why This Verse

Messianic prophecy quoted in Matthew

### Chapter Insight

This chapter foretells the coming ruler from Bethlehem. The key verse points to the Messiah who will shepherd His people in peace.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 6

<div class="key-verse">Micah 6:8</div>

<div class="identifier">What doth the LORD require of thee?</div>

### Why This Verse

One of the most quoted verses in the OT

### Chapter Insight

This chapter presents God's case against His people and calls for genuine obedience. The key verse summarizes God's desire for justice, mercy, and humble fellowship with Him.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 7

<div class="key-verse">Micah 7:8</div>

<div class="identifier">Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy</div>

### Why This Verse

Hope after failure

### Chapter Insight

This chapter moves from lament over sin to confidence in God's forgiveness and restoration. The key verse celebrates God's unmatched mercy toward repentant people.
:::
